newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian House passes tobacco restrictions bill.
newsitem.headline: Canadian House passes tobacco restrictions bill.

text.p: The Canadian House of Commons passed a bill on Thursday to restrict tobacco advertising and sponsorships despite protests from Quebec politicians over the effect it would have on cultural and sporting events.
The bill passed 139 to 37 and must now pass through Parliament's other chamber, the unelected Senate, where passage is by no means certain.

Senate aides said both Conservatives and Liberals would be raising questions about the bill's effect on freedom of expression and on sponsored events, though the sponsorship restrictions would not take effect until October 1998.
The bill would ban tobacco ads through broadcasting or billboards, ban tobacco sales through vending machines and restrict the use of tobacco brand names in sponsored events.

Health Minister David Dingwall wants to have the bill become law before a federal election, expected this spring or autumn. But senators have indicated they will take all the time they need to consider the bill.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain.
The second biggest player, Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, is owned 60 percent by Rothmans Inc, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Rothmans International Plc is owned by Swiss luxury goods holding company Cie Financiere Richmont AG.
Third place holder RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
